title: Out-of-sample reporter-to-biochemical calibration
question: Does corrected reporter AUC improve prediction of signed relative initial rates across held-out enzyme panels and held-out motif positions?
method: Frozen pooled OLS and increasing isotonic fits versus training means, leave-one-enzyme-out and leave-one-position-out across enzymes, excluding canonical keys. Reconcile deposited slopes and audit control inclusion.
result: Linear calibration beat the pooled training mean on all six enzyme panels and five of seven positions. Held-out P5 had substantial underprediction. The biochemical ratios use enzyme-by-position canonical controls.
limitations: Six selected related panels and single substitutions around one canonical motif.
Dimensionless control-normalized targets with shared denominators. No calibration to absolute kcat.
No joint unseen-enzyme/unseen-position test, folded-site test, proteome-wide test or replicate-level uncertainty.
Agent analysis with no human expert review.
